tei:div.tei:head: Psalm 127
tei:div.tei:p: In this Psalm David instructs Solomon, his son, on the virtues of proper training for children. The arrow shot from a strong hand bears within itself the strength of the bowman long after it has left his hand, and it follows unswervingly the direction given by the hand of the mighty man. So, too, children raised by dedicated parents will remain unwaveringly and unhesitat- ingly true to the goal set for them by the guiding hands of parents, long after they have left the immediate sphere of that parental guidance.A Song of Ascents of Solomon. If Adonoy will not build a house, then in vain have its builders toiled upon it; if Adonoy will not preserve the city, in vain does the watchman keep vigil. It is in vain for you that you rise early, sit up late, who eat the bread of toil; but He will surely give [sustenance] to His loved ones to those who banish sleep from themselves. Behold, a heritage of Adonoy, are children a reward [from Him] is the fruit of the womb. As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of one's youth. Fortunate is the man who has filled his quiver with them; they will not be ashamed when they speak with their enemies in the gate.
